en: 125(23.5) *The Sūtra on the Fragrance of the Virtue of Precepts* Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Tanwulan of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda was dwelling in seclusion and reflecting alone:

“In the world there are three kinds of fragrance: first, the fragrance of roots; second, the fragrance of branches; and third, the fragrance of flowers. These three types of fragrance travel only with the wind and cannot go against it. Is there perhaps a sublime fragrance that travels both with and against the wind?”

The venerable Ānanda, dwelling alone in seclusion, contemplated the meaning of this matter but could not discern its ultimate destination. He immediately rose from his seat, went to where the Buddha was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, knelt with palms joined, and addressed the Buddha, saying:

“While dwelling alone in seclusion, I contemplated that there are three kinds of fragrance in the world: first, the fragrance of roots; second, the fragrance of branches; and third, the fragrance of flowers. These three types of fragrance can only travel with the wind and cannot go against it. Is there perhaps a sublime fragrance that can travel both with and against the wind?”
The Buddha said to Ānanda:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
"It is exactly as you have asked: there is a fragrance that truly follows both with the wind and against the wind.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying, "I wish to hear about this fragrance."

The Buddha said: "If, in any commandery, kingdom, district, town, village, or hamlet, there is a son of good family or a daughter of good family who practices the ten wholesome paths—refraining from killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct with the body; refraining from false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, and frivolous speech with the mouth; and refraining from envy, malice, and delusion with the mind—who is filial and obedient to their parents, serves the Triple Gem, and possesses benevolence, compassion, moral virtue, majestic demeanor, and ritual propriety; then the śramaṇas and brahmins of the eastern direction will sing praises of their virtue, and the śramaṇas and brahmins of the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir will all sing of their virtue, saying:

'In such-and-such a commandery, kingdom, district, town, village, or hamlet, there is a son of good family or a daughter of good family who upholds the ten wholesome paths and reverently serves the Three Jewels; they are filial and compassionate, possessing moral virtue and a sense of duty, never failing in ritual propriety.'"

"This incense is named 'Pervading with the Wind'; there is nowhere it does not reach, whether with or against the wind, proclaiming virtue throughout the ten directions so that all may rely upon its grace.
At that time, the Buddha spoke in verse:
"Though there be fine fragrant flowers, They cannot perfume against the wind."
One who is tireless is named "Sandalwood," raining down all manner of fragrances.
With a mind that is harmonious and refined, one’s fragrance then wafts even against the wind;
such a true person is called a "Great Man" (Puruṣa), whose scent pervades the ten directions.
The fragrance of aloeswood and sandalwood, the scent of blue lotuses and various rains of incense—
of all these manifold fragrances, the fragrance of ethical discipline is supreme.
Those who are thus pure act without negligence.
Not knowing the path of Māra, one does not see where it leads.
This path leads to eternal peace; this path is supreme and unsurpassed.
By following it, one severs the source of defilement and subdues the snare of Māra.
By ascending to the Hall of the Buddha-way, one rises to infinite wisdom;
by means of this, one proclaims the meaning of the sutras and eliminates all evils.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"The diffusion of this fragrance is unimpeded by Mount Sumeru, mountains, rivers, or heaven and earth; it is unimpeded by the four elements of earth, water, fire, and wind; it penetrates the eight directions, and likewise above and below, such that throughout the infinite realms, all sing of its virtue."
If one refrains from killing throughout one's life, one will enjoy long life in every successive birth, and one’s life will not meet with untimely death.

One who does not steal will be wealthy and abundant in every successive birth; furthermore, their wealth and treasures will never be lost through negligence and will always remain, serving as the foundation for the Way.
Those who refrain from sexual misconduct do not violate the wives of others, and wherever they are reborn, they are born transformed within lotus flowers.
Those who refrain from false speech have fragrant breath, and their words are always trusted.
One who refrains from divisive speech ensures that families remain harmonious and free from separation.
One who refrains from harsh speech possesses a tongue always skilled in eloquent and effective discourse.
One who refrains from frivolous speech is such that all who hear their words consult, accept, and apply them as treasures.
One who is free from envy will be honored by all people in every lifetime they are born into.
One who is free from anger will be handsome in every lifetime, and people will rejoice upon seeing them.

One who has eliminated ignorance will possess wisdom such that there is no one they do not consult; having abandoned false views, they abide eternally in the Right Path. What is attained through practice arises spontaneously for each individual; therefore, one should discard the false and follow the true and wondrous.
Thus spoke the Buddha.
At that time, the bhikṣus, having heard this, rejoiced and paid homage before departing.
The Sūtra on the Fragrance of the Virtue of Precepts Spoken by the Buddha.
